Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 27-Dec-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2025  
  Software Engineering [IT_4061]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                     Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Analyze the evolution of software development from an art form to an engineering discipline. How         (5)  
  did this transformation impact software quality and maintainability?  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Apply the concepts of software process models to demonstrate how the Waterfall, Spiral, and Agile (5)  
  models differ in terms of flexibility, risk handling, and customer involvement.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                Examine how SSDLC extends the traditional SDLC and analyze its advantages in modern software (5)  
  development environments.  
  A)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Analyze how incomplete or ambiguous Software Requirement Specifications (SRS) can lead to                (5)  
  project failures. Illustrate with an example.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3)                Apply the concept of layered design architecture to demonstrate how it enhances system modularity (5)  
  and fault isolation in large-scale applications.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Construct a DFD model for a payroll management system that clearly shows the identification of           (5)  
  data transformations and process divisions.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Create"  
  
4)                Develop a software design model that applies structured design principles to show how complexity         (5)  
  can be reduced and maintainability enhanced.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Create"  
  
  B)           Analyze how different UML diagrams (use case, class, sequence) complement each other in                  (5)  
  representing a complete system design.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  Page #1

5)                       Evaluate the effectiveness of state-chart diagrams in modeling dynamic system behavior, using an    (5)  
  ATM transaction as an example.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
  B)               Assess the effectiveness of code review in complementing automated testing to improve software      (5)  
  reliability and maintainability.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
  
  -----End-----
